AKU → Storyblok · the complete folder and page tree

Every region, entity, department, centre, office and folder, and under each one every page with the address it has today and the address it will have. Children are listed in the order AKU’s own menus use — about, programmes, research, faculty, departments, then news, events and blogs — then everything else A–Z.

What each kind means

regionA country, or Global for what no country owns.7
entityA faculty, school or institute AKU lists under Academics or Research.29
departmentA unit with its own writers and approvers, confirmed on its own page.23
centreA standing unit inside a faculty that calls itself a centre.10
officeAn office inside a faculty — neither a department nor a programme.1
publicationSomething a unit publishes: a newsletter or a magazine.2
programmeA programme or project run by an entity.10
region folderA real unit at region level that AKU does not publish as an entity.5
sectionA top-level section of aku.edu that no faculty owns.38
folderAn ordinary folder.493
groupingA level Storyblok needs so the folder beneath it can exist. Holds no page of its own.9

What the tags mean

works in… The countries this unit’s own page says it operates in — which is deliberately not the same as the folder it sits in. The Brain & Mind Institute lives under global because no one country owns it, and works in Kenya and Pakistan. IED East Africa sits in east-africa, and its Development Projects work in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. The tag is the evidence for the placement, and it only appears where the answer changes from the folder above.
shared Content that belongs to a second entity as well as the one it is filed under. It gets one home folder and a tag for the other, rather than being duplicated. Hover to see which.
archive? The page names no recent edition — a conference last held in 2016, a magazine whose newest issue is 2020. Carrying it forward would publish it as current. Hover for what the page actually says.
ran 2024 An event microsite, and the most recent edition its own page names.
MC EA This folder sets its own permissions, and that is the team that administers it.
inherits · MC EA This folder sets no permissions of its own; whoever administers the nearest folder above it administers this one too.
